:::{#exr-bernoulli-likelihood-one-group}
#### Likelihood of binary outcomes with one event probability

A binary outcome $Y$ with event probability $\pi$ has

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(Y = 1) &= \pi
&& \text{(definition of the event probability)}\\
\Pr(Y = 0) &= 1 - \pi
&& \text{(complement rule)}\\
\Pr(Y = y) &= \pi^y (1 - \pi)^{1 - y}, \quad y \in \cb{0, 1}
&& \text{(combine the two cases)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\vy \eqdef (y_1, \ldots, y_n)$ be a dataset of
mutually independent binary outcomes,
all with the same event probability $\pi$:
$Y_i \simind \Ber(\pi)$.
Write the likelihood of $\vy$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-bernoulli-likelihood-one-group}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Lik(\pi; \vy)
&= \prod_{i=1}^n \Lik_i(\pi)
&& \text{(product of likelihood components)}\\
&= \prod_{i=1}^n \Pr(Y_i = y_i)
&& \text{(definition of likelihood components)}\\
&= \prodin \pi^{y_i} (1 - \pi)^{1 - y_i}
&& \text{(Bernoulli PMF)}\\
&= \paren{\prodin \pi^{y_i}} \paren{\prodin (1 - \pi)^{1 - y_i}}
&& \text{(regroup the factors of the product)}\\
&= \pi^{\sumin y_i} (1 - \pi)^{\sumin (1 - y_i)}
&& \text{(product of powers of a common base)}\\
&= \pi^{\sumin y_i} (1 - \pi)^{\sumin 1 - \sumin y_i}
&& \text{(split the sum in the exponent)}\\
&= \pi^{\sumin y_i} (1 - \pi)^{n - \sumin y_i}
&& \text{($\textstyle\sumin 1 = n$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
